correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all quantifiers p,q distinct primes with p≥3,k≥2 and character normalization p^{-1/2}. In Z[ζ_{q^k}]/(1−ζ_{q^k})≈F_q each q^k-root maps to 1, so a sum of exactly p such roots cannot vanish because q∤p. Since [Q(ζ_{pq^k}):Q(ζ_{q^k})]=p−1, Φ_p is irreducible over the q-power cyclotomic field and ∑_i c_iζ_p^{αi}=0 (α≠0) forces equal c_i. A spectral p-set's two-column difference cannot have α=0, and the equal nonzero c_i force every first residue represented exactly once; conversely transversals have p orthogonal characters (α,0). The exact zero set of its mask is α≠0 with β divisible by q^{k−t(f)}; unitary transpose forces every frequency basis to be a transversal B_g. Orthogonality is exactly t(f)+t(g)≥k, including t=0/k. Counting g(0) freely and p−1 congruent entries yields S(t)=q^{k+(p−1)t}; counting exact depths via exclusion yields N_t and summing gives (k+1)q^{k(p+1)}−kq^{k(p+1)−(p−1)}. Independent exact polynomial-remainder exhaustive checks of all unordered A,B for (3,2,1) boundary and (3,2,2) main domain found precisely 64 spectral A and 640 ordered pairs for latter; finite checks corroborate, not prove the unrestricted result.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the general repeated-prime-order p-cardinality pair compatibility and complete multiplicity/total-incidence census. Exact same submission is indexed in Resultary but not prior independent evidence. Published general Fourier-zero criteria and spectral/tiling equivalence do not state or directly imply the q^k-depth threshold plus all counts; the closest squarefree incidence theorem excludes k>=2, and the cyclic prime-fiber period theorem has a prime (not q^k) fiber and different graph size. The 2021 Fourier-submatrix primitive-set theorem covers nontrivial low-cardinality structural cases (notably 3x3) and is a serious incremental/priority overlap, but the inspected statement does not furnish all odd p, all q,k and all enumerators. Novelty qualified, not a certification of priority.

value.rationale: The full set of exact unweighted p-point Fourier spectral partners for every p-point subset of Z_{p q^k} is a natural, useful Hadamard-submatrix enumeration invariant, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The symmetric q-adic depth threshold gives a complete classification of all basis choices, with k+1 actually populated multiplicity strata S(t)=q^{k+(p−1)t}, their numbers N_t and the total incidence; distinct sets can have a spectrum ratio q^{k(p−1)} despite all having one basis. Prior existence/tiling theorems and the inspected squarefree/prime-fiber exact tables do not mechanically supply this repeated-prime spectrum census. Value is a focused exact refinement of classical cyclotomic tools, not a general Fuglede theorem, a novelty certificate, or a large downstream breakthrough.

final_claim: For distinct primes p≥3 and q and k≥2, a p-element subset of Z_p×Z_(q^k) has a p-character orthogonal Fourier basis iff it is a graph A_f over Z_p. The graph spectra B_g are exactly those satisfying t(f)+t(g)≥k; there are S(t)=q^{k+(p−1)t} spectra per set at depth t, N_t=q^k[q^{(k−t)(p−1)}−q^{(k−t−1)(p−1)}] for 0≤t<k and N_k=q^k such sets, and total (k+1)q^{k(p+1)}−kq^{k(p+1)−(p−1)} ordered spectral pairs.
limitations: Claim is unweighted prime-cardinality Fourier orthogonality on cyclic orders p q^k, k≥2 only; no general prime-power factor mix, arbitrary finite abelian group or weighted frames.
Complete exact finite tests cover only stated small parameter choices, not unrestricted p,q,k. Universal correctness rests on inspected cyclotomic and counting proof.
